sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 sits mid-range of its trailing month at 7,666.60 (Sept 2), between a 7,600.50 low and 7,798.99 high, up 0.87% over the period. The Nasdaq-100 is similarly mid-range at 29,143.33, up 1.27%. The VIX eased about 4% to 15.20, itself mid-range of a tight 14.25-16.50 band, so no volatility spike. The Euro Stoxx 50 is the outlier, closing at its one-month low of 6,362.15, down roughly 1%. This week's earnings load is light: five SP500/R1000 operating names report, concentrated in technology.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tue: DELL US reports into the technology cluster (503 tickers, flat +0.4% median 3-day reaction, heavy news flow) as the week's headline name. Wed: COO US reports into healthcare (452 tickers, muted +0.11% median) while SAIL US adds a second technology print the same day. Thu: ADBE US closes out the tech slate and KR US reports into consumer-defensive, the only one of the five sectors running negative this cycle at -0.71% median across 320 names. A diffuse, sector-spread week rather than a concentrated one.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.62% median across 160 tickers on a thick 2,628-item news window, with copper close behind at +2.63% median on 6 tickers. Oil-gas moves the other way at -2.205% median across 33 names on 1,014 news items. None of this week's five reporters sit in these three sectors, so this week's price action is more likely to hinge on the broader tape than on earnings-specific catalysts in the hottest sectors.
